tool.name: MS1LabeledWorkflow
tool.description: Quantification workflow for MS1-labeled (SILAC, Dimethyl, ...) LC-MS/MS experiments
tool.command:
@QUOTE_FOO@ @EXT_FOO@ #import re
## Preprocessing mkdir in_cond.in && #if $in_cond.in_select == "no" mkdir ${' '.join(["'in_cond.in/%s'" % (i) for i, f in enumerate($in_cond.in) if f])} && ${' '.join(["cp '%s' 'in_cond.in/%s/%s.%s' && " % (f, i, re.sub('[^\w\-_]', '_', f.element_identifier), $gxy2omsext(f.ext)) for i, f in enumerate($in_cond.in) if f])} #else cp '$in_cond.in' 'in_cond.in/${re.sub("[^\w\-_]", "_", $in_cond.in.element_identifier)}.$gxy2omsext($in_cond.in.ext)' && #end if mkdir ids_cond.ids && #if $ids_cond.ids_select == "no" mkdir ${' '.join(["'ids_cond.ids/%s'" % (i) for i, f in enumerate($ids_cond.ids) if f])} && ${' '.join(["cp '%s' 'ids_cond.ids/%s/%s.%s' && " % (f, i, re.sub('[^\w\-_]', '_', f.element_identifier), $gxy2omsext(f.ext)) for i, f in enumerate($ids_cond.ids) if f])} #else cp '$ids_cond.ids' 'ids_cond.ids/${re.sub("[^\w\-_]", "_", $ids_cond.ids.element_identifier)}.$gxy2omsext($ids_cond.ids.ext)' && #end if #if $design: mkdir design && cp '$design' 'design/${re.sub("[^\w\-_]", "_", $design.element_identifier)}.$gxy2omsext($design.ext)' && #end if #if $fasta: mkdir fasta && cp '$fasta' 'fasta/${re.sub("[^\w\-_]", "_", $fasta.element_identifier)}.$gxy2omsext($fasta.ext)' && #end if #if "out_FLAG" in str($OPTIONAL_OUTPUTS).split(',') mkdir out && #end if #if "out_cxml_FLAG" in str($OPTIONAL_OUTPUTS).split(',') mkdir out_cxml && #end if #if "out_qpx_FLAG" in str($OPTIONAL_OUTPUTS).split(',') mkdir out_qpx && #end if
## Main program call
set -o pipefail && @EXECUTABLE@ -write_ctd ./ && python3 '$__tool_directory__/fill_ctd.py' '@EXECUTABLE@.ctd' '$args_json' '$hardcoded_json' && @EXECUTABLE@ -ini @EXECUTABLE@.ctd -in #if $in_cond.in_select == "no" ${' '.join(["'in_cond.in/%s/%s.%s'"%(i, re.sub('[^\w\-_]', '_', f.element_identifier), $gxy2omsext(f.ext)) for i, f in enumerate($in_cond.in) if f])} #else 'in_cond.in/${re.sub("[^\w\-_]", "_", $in_cond.in.element_identifier)}.$gxy2omsext($in_cond.in.ext)' #end if -ids #if $ids_cond.ids_select == "no" ${' '.join(["'ids_cond.ids/%s/%s.%s'"%(i, re.sub('[^\w\-_]', '_', f.element_identifier), $gxy2omsext(f.ext)) for i, f in enumerate($ids_cond.ids) if f])} #else 'ids_cond.ids/${re.sub("[^\w\-_]", "_", $ids_cond.ids.element_identifier)}.$gxy2omsext($ids_cond.ids.ext)' #end if #if $design: -design 'design/${re.sub("[^\w\-_]", "_", $design.element_identifier)}.$gxy2omsext($design.ext)' #end if #if $fasta: -fasta 'fasta/${re.sub("[^\w\-_]", "_", $fasta.element_identifier)}.$gxy2omsext($fasta.ext)' #end if #if "out_FLAG" in str($OPTIONAL_OUTPUTS).split(',') -out 'out/output.${gxy2omsext("mztab")}' #end if #if "out_cxml_FLAG" in str($OPTIONAL_OUTPUTS).split(',') -out_cxml 'out_cxml/output.${gxy2omsext("consensusxml")}' #end if #if "out_qpx_FLAG" in str($OPTIONAL_OUTPUTS).split(',') -out_qpx out_qpx/ #end if #if len(str($OPTIONAL_OUTPUTS).split(',')) == 0 | tee '$stdout' #end if
## Postprocessing #if "out_FLAG" in str($OPTIONAL_OUTPUTS).split(',') && mv 'out/output.${gxy2omsext("mztab")}' '$out' #end if #if "out_cxml_FLAG" in str($OPTIONAL_OUTPUTS).split(',') && mv 'out_cxml/output.${gxy2omsext("consensusxml")}' '$out_cxml' #end if #if "ctd_out_FLAG" in $OPTIONAL_OUTPUTS && mv '@EXECUTABLE@.ctd' '$ctd_out' #end if

param.label: Experimental design (Fraction_Group, Fraction, Spectra_Filepath, Label, Sample), one row per (file, channel)
param.help: 'Label' is the 1-based position of the channel in '-labels'. If not given, every file is an unfractionated. fraction group and every (file, channel) is a separate sample select tabular data sets(s)

param.label: Protein database
param.help: If given, the identifications are re-indexed (PeptideIndexer): protein sequences (for coverage),. decoy annotation and theoretical peptide uniqueness (needed by 'strictly_unique_peptides') are taken from it select fasta data sets(s)

param.label: Labels used for labelling the samples, one bracket per channel
param.help: [...] specifies the labels for a single sample. For example. [][Lys8,Arg10] ... SILAC. [][Lys4,Arg6][Lys8,Arg10] ... triple-SILAC. [Dimethyl0][Dimethyl6] ... Dimethyl. [Dimethyl0][Dimethyl4][Dimethyl8] ... triple Dimethyl. [ICPL0][ICPL4][ICPL6][ICPL10] ... ICPL. The channels are numbered from 1 in this order ('Label' column of the experimental design)

param.label: Maximum number of labelled amino acids per peptide, minus one
param.help: Peptides with up to (this value + 1) labelled amino acids. are considered by feature detection and resolver. For SILAC with trypsin digestion, this is the maximum number of missed cleavages

param.label: Protein FDR threshold (0.05=5%)
Use a picked protein FDR?
FDR threshold for sub-protein level
param.help: (e.g. 0.05=5%). Use -FDR_type to choose the level. Cutoff is applied at the highest level

param.label: Sub-protein FDR level
param.help: PSM, PSM+peptide (best PSM q-value)

param.label: Infer proteins:
param.help: aggregation = aggregates all peptide scores across a protein (using the best score) . bayesian = computes a posterior probability for every protein based on a Bayesian network

param.label: true: keep multiplets without an identification, so that linking can hand them the identification of a multiplet at the
param.help: same position in another run (the counterpart of ProteomicsLFQ's '-targeted_only false').. false: only identified multiplets are quantified.. Cannot be combined with 'algorithm:knock_out': the channel order of an unidentified multiplet is only known from its detection pattern

param.name: charge
param.label: Range of charge states in the sample
param.help: i.e. min charge : max charge

param.name: isotopes_per_peptide
param.label: Range of isotopes per peptide in the sample
param.help: For example 3:6, if isotopic peptide patterns in the sample consist of either three, four, five or six isotopic peaks.

param.name: rt_typical
param.label: Typical retention time [s] over which a characteristic peptide elutes
param.help: (This is not an upper bound. Peptides that elute for longer will be reported.)

param.name: rt_band
param.label: The algorithm searches for characteristic isotopic peak patterns, spectrum by spectrum
param.help: For some low-intensity peptides, an important peak might be missing in one spectrum but be present in one of the neighbouring ones. The algorithm takes a bundle of neighbouring spectra with width rt_band into account. For example with rt_band = 0, all characteristic isotopic peaks have to be present in one and the same spectrum. As rt_band increases, the sensitivity of the algorithm but also the likelihood of false detections increases

param.name: rt_min
param.label: Lower bound for the retention time [s]
param.help: (Any peptides seen for a shorter time period are not reported.)

param.name: mz_tolerance
param.label: m/z tolerance for search of peak patterns

param.name: mz_unit
param.label: Unit of the 'mz_tolerance' paramete

param.name: intensity_cutoff
param.label: Lower bound for the intensity of isotopic peaks

param.name: peptide_similarity
param.label: Two peptides in a multiplet are expected to have the same isotopic pattern
param.help: This parameter is a lower bound on their similarity

param.name: averagine_similarity
param.label: The isotopic pattern of a peptide should resemble the averagine model at this m/z position
param.help: This parameter is a lower bound on similarity between measured isotopic pattern and the averagine model

param.name: averagine_similarity_scaling
param.label: Let x denote this scaling factor, and p the averagine similarity paramete
param.help: For the detection of single peptides, the averagine parameter p is replaced by p' = p + x(1-p), i.e. x = 0 -> p' = p and x = 1 -> p' = 1. (For knock_out = true, peptide doublets and singlets are detected simultaneously. For singlets, the peptide similarity filter is irreleavant. In order to compensate for this 'missing filter', the averagine parameter p is replaced by the more restrictive p' when searching for singlets.)

param.name: spectrum_type
param.label: Type of MS1 spectra in input mzML file
param.help: 'automatic' determines the spectrum type directly from the input mzML file

param.name: averagine_type
param.label: The type of averagine to use, currently RNA, DNA or peptide

param.name: knock_out
param.label: Is it likely that knock-outs are present
param.help: (Supported for doublex, triplex and quadruplex experiments only.)

section.name: alignment
section.title: Parameters of the identification-based retention time alignment (MapAlignerIdentification)

param.name: score_type
param.label: Name of the score type to use for ranking and filtering (.oms input only)
param.help: If left empty, a score type is picked automatically

param.name: score_cutoff
param.label: Use only IDs above a score cut-off (parameter 'min_score') for alignment?

param.name: min_score
param.label: If 'score_cutoff' is 'true': Minimum score for an ID to be considered
param.help: Unless you have very few runs or identifications, increase this value to focus on more informative peptides

param.name: min_run_occur
param.label: Minimum number of runs (incl
param.help: reference, if any) in which a peptide must occur to be used for the alignment.. Unless you have very few runs or identifications, increase this value to focus on more informative peptides

param.name: max_rt_shift
param.label: Maximum realistic RT difference for a peptide (median per run vs
param.help: reference). Peptides with higher shifts (outliers) are not used to compute the alignment.. If 0, no limit (disable filter); if > 1, the final value in seconds; if <= 1, taken as a fraction of the range of the reference RT scale

param.name: use_unassigned_peptides
param.label: Should unassigned peptide identifications be used when computing an alignment of feature or consensus maps
param.help: If 'false', only peptide IDs assigned to features will be used

param.name: use_feature_rt
param.label: When aligning feature or consensus maps, don't use the retention time of a peptide identification directly; instead, use the retention time of the centroid of the feature (apex of the elution profile) that the peptide was matched to
param.help: If different identifications are matched to one feature, only the peptide closest to the centroid in RT is used.. Precludes 'use_unassigned_peptides'

param.name: use_adducts
param.label: If IDs contain adducts, treat differently adducted variants of the same molecule as different

param.name: auto_reference
param.label: Reference to align to if none is given (neither a reference file nor an input index): 'best_run' - the input that shares the most identified sequences with every other input (on ties, the one with the most identified sequences)
param.help: A consensus is used instead if no input shares at least two sequences with every other input. If the chosen input leaves other inputs with too few alignment points, other inputs and a consensus are tried as well (see 'auto_reference_min_points'). 'consensus' - median RTs per sequence over all inputs. A consensus favors none of the inputs, but only partly corrects larger RT shifts, because every input contributes to the consensus it is aligned to

param.name: auto_reference_min_points
param.label: If 'auto_reference' is 'best_run': number of alignment points (after removing outliers, see 'max_rt_shift') that the reference should provide for every other input
param.help: If the chosen input leaves inputs with fewer points, and one of them shares at least this many sequences with other inputs, every input and a consensus of all inputs are tried as the reference. The choice that gives the most inputs at least this many points is used (the reference counts); on ties, the first choice is kept, and an input is preferred over a consensus. The default is the smallest number of points to which ProteomicsLFQ and MS1LabeledWorkflow fit an RT model. 0 disables the check

section.name: linking
section.title: Parameters for linking the multiplets across runs (FeatureLinkerUnlabeledQT)

param.name: use_identifications
param.label: Never link features that are annotated with different peptides (only the best hit per peptide identification is taken into account)

param.name: nr_partitions
param.label: How many partitions in m/z space should be used for the algorithm (more partitions means faster runtime and more memory efficient execution)

param.name: min_nr_diffs_per_bin
param.label: If IDs are used: How many differences from matching IDs should be used to calculate a linking tolerance for unIDed features in an RT region
param.help: RT regions will be extended until that number is reached

param.name: min_IDscore_forTolCalc
param.label: If IDs are used: What is the minimum score of an ID to assume a reliable match for tolerance calculation
param.help: Check your current score type!

param.name: noID_penalty
param.label: If IDs are used: For the normalized distances, how high should the penalty for missing IDs be
param.help: 0 = no bias, 1 = IDs inside the max tolerances always preferred (even if much further away)

param.name: ignore_charge
param.label: false [default]: pairing requires equal charge state (or at least one unknown charge '0'); true: Pairing irrespective of charge state

param.name: ignore_adduct
param.label: true [default]: pairing requires equal adducts (or at least one without adduct annotation); true: Pairing irrespective of adducts

section.name: distance_RT
section.title: Distance component based on RT differences

param.name: exponent
param.label: Normalized RT differences ([0-1], relative to 'max_difference') are raised to this power (using 1 or 2 will be fast, everything else is REALLY slow)

param.name: weight
param.label: Final RT distances are weighted by this facto

section.name: distance_MZ
section.title: Distance component based on m/z differences

param.name: max_difference
param.label: Never pair features with larger m/z distance (unit defined by 'unit')

param.name: unit
param.label: Unit of the 'max_difference' paramete

param.name: exponent
param.label: Normalized ([0-1], relative to 'max_difference') m/z differences are raised to this power (using 1 or 2 will be fast, everything else is REALLY slow)

param.name: weight
param.label: Final m/z distances are weighted by this facto

section.name: distance_intensity
section.title: Distance component based on differences in relative intensity (usually relative to highest peak in the whole data set)

param.name: exponent
param.label: Differences in relative intensity ([0-1]) are raised to this power (using 1 or 2 will be fast, everything else is REALLY slow)

param.name: weight
param.label: Final intensity distances are weighted by this facto

param.name: log_transform
param.label: Log-transform intensities
param.help: If disabled, d = |int_f2 - int_f1| / int_max. If enabled, d = |log(int_f2 + 1) - log(int_f1 + 1)| / log(int_max + 1))

section.name: ProteinQuantification
section.title: Parameters of the peptide and protein abundances (ProteinQuantifier)

param.name: method
param.label: - top - quantify based on three most abundant peptides (number can be changed in 'top')
param.help: - iBAQ (intensity based absolute quantification), calculate the sum of all peptide peak intensities divided by the number of theoretically observable tryptic peptides (https://rdcu.be/cND1J). Warning: only consensusXML or featureXML input is allowed!

param.name: best_charge
param.label: Distinguish between fraction and charge states in detailed peptide output
param.help: For protein quantification, select one charge per modified peptide globally: maximize the number of (fraction group, label) assays with a positive abundance, then break ties by total abundance; retain that charge's values in every assay.. By default, protein abundances are summed over all charge states. How the retained values of several fractions are combined is governed by 'fractions:aggregate', not by this flag

section.name: top
section.title: Additional options for custom quantification using top N peptides

param.name: N
param.label: Calculate protein abundance from this number of proteotypic peptides (most abundant first; '0' for all)

param.name: aggregate
param.label: Aggregation method used to compute protein abundances from peptide abundances

param.name: include_all
param.label: Include results for proteins with fewer proteotypic peptides than indicated by 'N' (no effect if 'N' is 0 or 1)

section.name: fractions
section.title: Options for combining the fractions of a fraction group

param.name: aggregate
param.label: How the fractions of one fraction group are combined into that group's (fraction group, label) assay values
param.help: - sum - add up every fraction, i.e. treat them as the parts of one separated sample that they are.. - best - keep a single fraction per peptide and fraction group and discard the others. The fraction is chosen ONCE per peptide, ranked by the number of labels in which it has a positive abundance and then by the total of those abundances (an exact tie keeps the lowest fraction number), and ALL of its labels are then taken from it. The choice is deliberately not made per label: taking one channel from one fraction and another channel from a different fraction would mix physical aliquots and destroy the reporter-ion ratios that isobaric quantification consists of.. Only the assay values are affected. Per-(file, channel) quantities are per fraction by definition and always report every file

section.name: consensus
section.title: Additional options for consensus maps (and identification results comprising multiple runs)

param.name: normalize
param.label: Scale peptide abundances so that the median of each (fraction group, label) assay matches the overall median
param.help: Abundances of zero count as 'not detected' and are left out of the medians; an assay without any positive abundance takes no part in the normalization

param.name: fix_peptides
param.label: Use the same peptides for protein quantification across all (fraction group, label) assays
param.help: With 'N 0',all peptides that occur in every assay are considered.. Otherwise ('N'), the N peptides that occur in the most assays (independently of each other) are selected,. breaking ties by total abundance (there is no guarantee that the best co-ocurring peptides are chosen!).. A peptide counts as occurring in an assay only where its abundance is positive: an abundance stored as zero means 'not detected' (e.g. an isobaric reporter below 'min_reporter_intensity'), not a measurement of absence

section.name: ratios
section.title: Parameters of the channel ratios, the reported quantity of a labeled experiment

param.name: reference_channel
param.label: Channel the ratios are formed against, as the 'Label' of the experimental design (1 = the light channel of '-labels')

param.name: min_ratio_count
param.label: Minimum number of peptide ratios a protein group needs before a ratio is reported for it (MaxQuant's 'min
param.help: ratio count'). Groups below it are reported without a ratio, not with a less certain one

param.name: normalize
param.label: Additionally report every ratio divided by the median peptide ratio of its (fraction group, channel)
param.help: i.e. assuming that most peptides do not change. The unnormalized ratios are reported either way

param.label: Quantify proteins based on:
param.help: unique_peptides = use peptides mapping to single proteins or a group of indistinguishable proteins(according to the set of experimentally identified peptides).. strictly_unique_peptides = use peptides mapping to a unique single protein only.. shared_peptides = use shared peptides only for its best group (by inference score)

param.label: Overrides tool-specific checks
Enables the test mode (needed for internal use only)
